body:
I think it's safe to assume that AT can handle string values (due to the existing content attributes) and element references (due to that being implemented, but not yet defined).

From that perspective it makes sense to me to try to generalize the reflect primitive to work for `Element` and `ElementInternals`.

How to generalize reflect:

* We require that objects that want to support reflect for their IDL attributes have a "get content attribute" and "set content attribute" operation.
* All the reflect algorithms are updated to use these operations.
* `ElementInternals` uses these operations to update its "native accessibility semantics map".
* `Element` uses these operations to get and set attributes as per the DOM standard.
* For `Element?` and `FrozenArray<Element>?` `ElementInternals` would need the associated concepts as well of course, both for bookkeeping and exposing to AT. For those attributes the "native accessibility semantics map" ends up being somewhat pointless. We could try to do more clever things here if we wanted to, but I think it make some sense to stay close to how `Element` solves this to keep the mental model simpler.

If that plan makes sense I'm happy to work on it, might have to wait a little bit due to other commitments. Thoughts?

> I think it's safe to assume that AT can handle string values (due to the existing content attributes) and element references (due to that being implemented, but not yet defined).

This is an interesting way of slicing the problem. It definitely reduces some complexity by avoiding solving the longstanding issue of how ARIA-provided strings are actually processed. For example, there is no spec today to my knowledge for what happens if you do `aria-checked="asdf"` or `aria-checked="   true "` or even `aria-checked="TRUE"`. It'd be nice if we didn't have to solve that at the same time.

With that in mind, here's how I think this might be defined if we were starting from scratch. We'd be targeting a `getTheCurrent(X, element)` where `X` is one of `role`, `aria-checked`, `aria-labelledby`, etc. This does:

1. If the element has an [X-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-associated-element), then return it. (Even if it's null.)

1. Otherwise, if the element's native accessibility semantics map\[X] exists, then return it.

1. Otherwise, return the default value for X.

The problem is then about ensuring the native accessibility semantics map has the correct thing, when the ElementInternals property is a non-string and non-element. For this I don't think we need to generalize reflect. We just need an algorithm for converting non-string non-elements into either strings or elements. (In practice, we just need an algorithm for converting numbers into strings.)

This seems a good bit simpler than what you describe, and doesn't mean changing reflect which is somewhat foundational. What do you think?

We discussed this a bunch more on Matrix: https://matrixlogs.bakkot.com/WHATWG/2022-10-28.

TL;DR: there's quite a bit of redundancy in my approach as `ElementInternals` doesn't require an as complicated setup, so we'll want to explain that it's done that way to ensure API consistency as well as making it easier to define new attributes (no special care needed for `ElementInternals`).
There's now a draft for this work: #8496. (Early days still, but would appreciate feedback on the approach.)
Sorry I'm not finding the time to review this properly, let's add @alice in the loop to see if she can dig into this.

I had a chat with Anne about this issue to try and clarify the goals of this work, since I was having trouble following them from the issue alone.

This work began as Anne noticed some potential issues with the way `ARIAMixin` is used on `ElementInternals`:

- `Element`/`FrozenArray<Element>` attributes are set directly with no checking of Shadow DOM, and in fact not even any checking whether the related element is even in the same document
- Also, `ElementInternals` has no equivalent to the [cached _attr_-associated elements](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#cached-attr-associated-elements) mechanism used on `Element` "to preserve the invariant that `element.reflectedElements === element.reflectedElements`"
- It's not clear what the getters on `ElementInternals` for the  `ARIAMixin` attributes should return when the value is missing - there is no equivalent to the missing value default for content attributes
- There is a potential maintenance burden when new attributes (attribute types?) are added to `ARIAMixin`

So, the refactoring in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/8496 aims to address these issues by making `ElementInternals`' `ARIAMixin` attributes use the same logic as content attribute reflection:

- since it will go through the same logic, shadow DOM and same document checking and will happen automatically; likewise, the implementation details around caching values will be carried across
- similarly, missing value defaults will be equivalent between content attributes and `ElementInternals`
- and any new attributes/attribute types will only need to define their validation rules in one place.

During our discussion I questioned whether it was necessary to hide elements in shadow DOM from `ElementInternals` the way we do for the "public" DOM API. Anne agreed that it might not be necessary given that `ElementInternals` is, like shadow DOM itself, intended to be a private API for custom elements to use for their own implementation details, so the risks of exposing implementation details are much less of a concern. There is now a [separate issue](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8544) for that.

I also wondered what the most useful thing might be in the case where no value has been set on `ElementInternals` for an `ARIAMixin` attribute, and an author calls the getter; this will depend on how Custom Element authors will want to interact with `ElementInternals`. 

We also need to specify what the [**native accessibility semantics map**](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#native-accessibility-semantics-map) exposes to accessibility API mapping logic when there is a missing value. Anne's proposed solution also handles this automatically.

I definitely agree that the process of adding new ARIA/`ARIAMixin` attributes should be as streamlined as possible, so I'm going to take some time to think through what is required in the current set-up to add new attributes, and how else we might make that easier. And similarly, that any critical validation that occurs as part of the reflection logic and needs to also happen on `ElementInternals` shouldn't need to be updated in two places.

Anne also noted as we were talking that it's not clear how the [cached _attr_-associated elements](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#cached-attr-associated-elements) mechanism for `FrozenArray<Element>` is garbage-collected. ([Issue](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8545).)
The refactoring PR is finally in a state that's more or less ready. Additional review appreciated.
